title: Synchronizing Genomic Model Weights
business: Bioinformatics teams managing large-scale genomic sequence model weights.
problem: Git repositories become bloated and unusable when storing multi-gigabyte model weight files, leading to slow clones and repository corruption.
solution: DVC decouples large model files from Git by storing them in external remote storage while keeping lightweight metadata pointers in the repository.
steps: Initialize DVC within the existing Git repository using dvc init.
Add the large model weight file to DVC tracking using dvc add, which generates a small .dvc metadata file.
Configure a remote storage location, such as S3 or a shared network drive, using dvc remote add.
Push the actual model data to the remote storage with dvc push.
Commit the .dvc metadata file to Git to version the model state alongside the training code.
outcome: Developers can clone the repository instantly and retrieve specific model versions on demand without bloating the Git history.
limitation: DVC is not designed for data lakes or petabyte-scale storage; performance may degrade when syncing tens of thousands of individual files, requiring alternative infrastructure solutions.

questions.question: In Synchronizing Genomic Model Weights, how does DVC resolve the issue of repository bloat?
options: By compressing all files into a single Git blob
By storing large files in external remote storage and tracking metadata in Git
By automatically deleting old model versions from the server
By forcing developers to use a separate Git repository for every model
questions.explanation: DVC decouples large model files from Git by storing them in external remote storage while keeping lightweight metadata pointers in the repository.

It prevents developers from switching between different model versions
